en: The Philippine eagle has a wingspan of up to two meters, making it one of the largest and rarest forest eagles in the world.
The Philippine Declaration of Independence was proclaimed on June 12, 1898, by Emilio Aguinaldo in Kawit, Cavite, ending over 300 years of Spanish rule.
The Philippine government has three co-equal branches: the executive, legislative, and judicial, with the Supreme Court composed of exactly 15 justices.
The Philippines has over 180 distinct living languages, but Filipino and English are the two official languages used in government and education.
The Philippine archipelago consists of exactly 7,641 islands, which are divided into three main geographical divisions: Luzon, Visayas, and Mindanao.
Jose Rizal was only 35 years old when he was executed by firing squad at Bagumbayan on December 30, 1896.
The Sinulog Festival in Cebu honors the Santo Niño, featuring a grand parade with thousands of dancers moving to a two-beat drum rhythm.
The Banaue Rice Terraces, built by the Ifugao people over 2,000 years ago, reach up to 1,500 meters above sea level.
Dr. Fe del Mundo became the first female student admitted to Harvard Medical School in 1936.
The Philippines is home to over 1,100 native orchid species, including the rare Vanda sanderiana, known locally as the Waling-waling.
Filipino citizens must be at least 18 years old and properly registered to vote in all national and local elections.
Juan Luna's famous painting Spoliarium measures 4.22 meters by 7.64 meters and won the first gold medal at the 1884 Madrid Exposition.
